title: VVS Laxman Set To Be Named BCCI's First Director of Cricket
excerpt: The newly created role places Laxman above head coach Gambhir and chief selector Agarkar in the hierarchy, unifying oversight across all levels of Indian cricket.
body:
• VVS Laxman is set to be appointed as the BCCI's first-ever Director of Cricket, a newly created position that will place him above head coach Gautam Gambhir and chief selector Ajit Agarkar in the hierarchy.
  • The appointment comes with a two-year contract extension at the Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru, where Laxman has been managing junior cricket development, player rehabilitation, and talent pathways.
  • Both Gambhir and Agarkar are expected to retain their current roles through the 2027 ODI World Cup, but the new structure formalizes oversight of all Indian cricket operations under Laxman.

VVS Laxman, currently the head of the BCCI's Centre of Excellence (CoE) in Bengaluru, is set to be named the board's first Director of Cricket — a newly created position that will reshape the hierarchy of Indian cricket administration, according to sources who spoke to NDTV.

The appointment comes with a two-year contract extension and gives Laxman formal authority over staff appointments across Indian cricket. While he will continue handling his existing responsibilities at the CoE — overseeing junior teams, player rehabilitation, and development pathways for both men's and women's cricket — the new designation creates a structured link between every tier of the system, from senior coaches and selectors to youth programs.

What It Means for Gambhir and Agarkar

The timing of the announcement raises questions about the futures of two key figures in Indian cricket. Chief selector Ajit Agarkar's tenure is set to expire in September, and his recent decisions — particularly regarding the ODI futures of Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli — have drawn scrutiny from the BCCI's top brass.

Head coach Gautam Gambhir's position has also been a subject of discussion. While Gambhir guided India to the 2026 T20 World Cup title and has an excellent white-ball record, India's poor positioning in the World Test Championship points table has kept pressure on his red-ball coaching future. The upcoming two-match Test series against Sri Lanka is seen as a critical test.

Sources confirmed to NDTV that the Director of Cricket role effectively places Laxman above both Gambhir and Agarkar in the organizational structure. However, there is no immediate risk to either position — both are expected to retain their roles through the 2027 ODI World Cup in South Africa, Zimbabwe, and Namibia.

"The revised role virtually puts Laxman above Team India head coach Gautam Gambhir and selection committee chief Ajit Agarkar. However, there is no risk to Agarkar and Gambhir's immediate future."

— NDTV Sources

Laxman's Track Record

Laxman has been a steady presence behind the scenes in Indian cricket since taking over the Centre of Excellence in 2021, succeeding Rahul Dravid. At the CoE, he has managed the coaching structure, education programs, and sports science department while playing a key role in developing Under-19 cricketers who feed into the senior talent pipeline.

He has also served as India's interim head coach on multiple occasions, most recently leading the team in a three-match T20I series against Zimbabwe. Gambhir himself acknowledged Laxman's contributions after the T20 World Cup triumph, saying he dedicated the trophy in part to Laxman "for unconditionally doing so much for Indian cricket, especially behind the doors, because CoE remains the pipeline for Indian cricket."

Laxman's name has repeatedly surfaced for higher roles. After Dravid's coaching contract ended in 2024, Laxman was considered for the head coach position before the BCCI chose Gambhir. Following India's Test series losses to New Zealand and South Africa, the board explored a split-coaching model with Laxman as Test coach, though those discussions didn't materialize.

A Structural Shift for Indian Cricket

The Director of Cricket role represents a significant organizational evolution for the BCCI. Rather than having coaches, selectors, and development programs operate as largely independent verticals, the new structure creates a single point of coordination. Laxman's deep involvement across all levels of Indian cricket — from grassroots development to senior team support — makes him a natural fit for the position.

The move also signals the BCCI's intent to create more formal institutional structures around talent development, rather than relying on ad hoc arrangements. With India's cricket calendar becoming increasingly packed and the pressure for results across all three formats intensifying, having a unified approach to player development and staff management could prove essential for maintaining the team's competitive edge.
